title: Rhombus Botnet Investigation
description: Investigate and contain the Rhombus botnet (Linux/IRCTelnet) infection on compromised systems.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are a cybersecurity analyst responding to reports of unusual network traffic from internal systems.

The Rhombus botnet (Linux/IRCTelnet) has been detected in your network, targeting VPS and IoT devices.

Your task is to investigate the compromised systems, identify the command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
SSH access to bot1 with user credentials provided.

From bot1, you can SSH to bot2 using the established trust relationship.

You have sudo privileges on both bot1 and bot2.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious beacon service
levels.content:
Investigate the systemd services running on bot1.

Identify the service responsible for beaconing to the C2 server.

The service name will be your flag.
levels.solution:
1. List all systemd services: `systemctl list-units --type=service`
2. Look for services with unusual names or descriptions related to system health or updates.
3. The service name is `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions related to system health or updates.

levels.title: Identify the persistence mechanism
levels.content:
Examine the systemd timers and services on bot1.

Identify the service responsible for maintaining persistence.

The service name will be your flag.
levels.solution:
1. List all systemd timers: `systemctl list-timers`
2. Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions related to system updates or health checks.
3. The service name is `system-update-checker.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions related to system updates or health checks.

levels.title: Contain the C2 communication
levels.content:
Identify the C2 server IP address and port from the beacon service configuration.

Implement a firewall rule to block outbound connections to the C2 server.

The port number used to block the connection will be your flag.
levels.solution:
1. Check the beacon script or service configuration for the C2 server details.
2. The C2 server IP address is `192.168.70.5` and the port is `2222`.
3. Implement a firewall rule to block outbound connections to the C2 server: `iptables -A OUTPUT -d 192.168.70.5 -p tcp --destination-port 2222 -j DROP`.
